title: BPS employed persons by status in the main job, by province, Sakernas Februari and Agustus rounds, 2017S1-2026S1, Indonesia

columns.province_code: BPS province code (kode_bps); 00 = Indonesia. Names and Kemendagri codes in 'provinces'.
columns.work_status: Status in the main job (status pekerjaan utama), BPS's seven statuses and their TOTAL; names in 'work_status'.
columns.period: YYYYS1 = the Februari round of Sakernas in year YYYY, YYYYS2 = the Agustus round (see 'periods').
columns.status: Revision marker; the table note states none, so every row is empty (final).
columns.value: Persons (Orang), whole persons as BPS publishes them. Multiply by 'multiplier' for base units.

province_source.note: BPS and Kemendagri codes differ for the six Papua provinces; join other datasets on the code system they use. Every region label in the table matches the BPS list after cleaning.normalise_name, so no alias is declared.

hidden_cells.reason: Note line 2: '2. Data yang kosong menandakan bahwa nilai RSE ≥ 50%, sehingga data tidak ditampilkan' (an empty cell has a relative standard error of 50% or more and is not shown). 21 cells are empty for this reason; each has no row.

coverage.indonesia: The table lists Indonesia (row 9999 'INDONESIA') after the 38 provinces, with a value in every status and round; it is written as code 00.

borders: 65 (Kalimantan Utara) has its own values in every round held, so 64 (Kalimantan Timur) excludes it.
91 (Papua Barat) and 94 (Papua) up to 2023 cover the areas before the 2022 split: the table gives 92, 95, 96 and 97 no value before 2024. From 2024, 91 and 94 cover the provinces after the split.

Counts add across provinces, so an area of several provinces, such as Papua Barat before the split (91 + 92) or Papua (94 + 95 + 96 + 97), is the sum of its provinces' values from 2024, except where a cell is hidden.
A change of 91 or 94 from 2023 to 2024 compares different areas; the change checks leave those changes out (checks.change_not_compared).

source_table.note_reading: The note's source line names only the 2025 rounds and its publication line the 2026 publication, though the table holds 2017-2026; its third line defines industry (lapangan usaha, KBLI 2025), a breakdown this table does not have. source_table.request: https://webapi.bps.go.id/v1/api/list/model/data/domain/0000/var/2335/th/{th}/key/{key} (th = first:last year minus 1900, such as 117:119 for 2017-2019; the key is not stored)

notes: No other raw file in the repository holds these counts, so there is no cross-source check (layer 4).
Indonesia's values are BPS's own national figures, not computed here; the provinces add to them to the person in every status and round of 2017-2025 (checks.identities).

The Februari 2026 round does not add up: in ten provinces the published statuses exceed TOTAL, and in three statuses the provinces exceed Indonesia, by up to 869,515 persons. The values are kept as published and the gaps declared (checks.identities, declared_gaps); a later BPS release is filed as a new raw file.
Derived values are not stored. Share of a status in employment (%) = status / TOTAL x 100; change from the same round a year before (%) = (value in t / value in t-1 - 1) x 100.
checks.flags lists every value or change outside its range in checks.plausible_ranges for a person to review; a flag stays whether it reflects a real event or a source error.

identities.check: the seven statuses add to TOTAL (key: region, round)
the provinces add to Indonesia (key: status, round)

checks.cross_source: Not applicable (layer 4): no other raw file holds these values; see 'notes'.

total_change_pct.measure: Change of TOTAL from the same region's same round a year before, in percent ((TOTAL in t / TOTAL in t-1 - 1) x 100). Employment grows with the working-age population and seldom moves more than a few percent a year, so a fall of more than 10 percent or a rise of more than 15 percent is flagged for review.

employee_change_pct.measure: Change of employee from the same region's same round a year before, in percent. Employees are a sample estimate that moves more than all employment in a small province, so only a fall of more than 20 percent or a rise of more than 30 percent is flagged for review.

employee_share_pct.measure: Employees as a percent of TOTAL in the same region and round (employee / TOTAL x 100). Below 3 or above 80 would lie far outside the provinces' values (checks.plausibility_observed), so it is flagged for review.
